गया. सर्कुलर में कहा गया कि गृह मंत्रालय ने विरोध-प्रदर्शन के लिए वैकल्पिक जगहों की जांच करने के लिए एक समिति बनाई थी, और उसी की सिफारिश के आधार पर यह फैसला हुआ. जंतर-मंतर को गैर-अधिसूचित (De-notified) कर दिया गया. वहीं रामलीला ग्राउंड, बुराड़ी ग्राउंड और पूर्वी दिल्ली का सीबीडी ग्राउंड नए स्थल बताए गए. दिल्ली पुलिस की तरफ से जारी सर्कुलर गृह मंत्रालय का जवाब. हालांकि, पुलिस की तरफ से जारी इस सर्कुलर में समिति के सदस्यों, उसकी सिफारिश और उसके गठन की तारीख का कोई ब्योरा नहीं था. जिसके बाद न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री ने 13 अक्टूबर को सूचना के अधिकार के तहत गृह मंत्रालय में एक अर्जी दी. इस आरटीआई अर्जी में समिति के गठन और उसके सदस्यों से जुड़ी जानकारी मांगी गई थी. साथ ही, समिति की बैठकों और उसकी सिफारिशों की प्रतियां भी मांगी गई. इसके अलावा, जंतर-मंतर को प्रदर्शन स्थल की सूची से हटाने के आदेश, इसके पीछे दर्ज कारणों और संबंधित सरकारी पत्राचार की प्रतियां मांगी गई थीं. गृह मंत्रालय के केंद्रशासित प्रदेश (यूटी) प्रभाग के केंद्रीय जन सूचना अधिकारी (सीपीआईओ) रवि कुमार चौधरी ने हमारी अर्जी के जवाब में कहा कि जानकारी का स्वरूप और उसके खुलासे के संभावित प्रभावों को देखते हुए इसे आरटीआई अधिनियम, 2005 की धारा 8 (1) (a) के तहत छूट प्राप्त है. मालूम हो कि आरटीआई अधिनियम की धारा 8(1)(a) ऐसी जानकारी के खुलासे से छूट देती है, जिससे भारत की संप्रभुता और अखंडता, राज्य की सुरक्षा, रणनीतिक, वैज्ञानिक या आर्थिक हित, या विदेशी राज्य से संबंध प्रभावित हो सकते हैं, या जो किसी अपराध के लिए उकसावे का कारण बन सकती है. सवाल उठता है कि जंतर-मंतर को प्रदर्शन स्थल से हटाने और नए प्रदर्शन स्थलों की पहचान के लिए बनी कमेटी का कामकाज सुरक्षा हित से कैसे जुड़ा है? आरटीआई कानून के लिए संघर्ष करने वाले मजदूर किसान शक्ति संगठन (एमकेएसएस) के निखिल डे इसके जवाब में कहते हैं, "'सुरक्षा' के कारण जवाब न देना.. दिखाता है कि सरकार का रवैया क्या है. समिति में कौन हैं, हम कहां प्रदर्शन कर सकते हैं, यह सब items.title: Who suggested de-notifying Jantar Mantar as a protest site? Govt gives no answer, cites national security
items.summary: Amidst protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and various opposition parties demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar last month, the Delhi Police issued a circular. Dated October 11, the Delhi Police Standing Order, signed by Commissioner Anurag Kumar, de-notified Jantar Mantar as a protest site and designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi in its place. The order said the decision was based on the recommendations of a committee constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs to examine “alternative proper venues” for citizens to hold protests and demonstrations in place of the existing “designated site”. The circular contained no details about the committee’s members, the specific recommendations made, or the date the committee was formed, among other details. On October 13, Newslaundry filed a Right to Information (RTI) application with the Ministry of Home Affairs, posing four questions, including: - A certified copy of the order constituting the committee tasked with identifying alternative protest sites in Delhi, and the date on which it was formed. - The names, designations and departments of the committee’s chairperson and all its members, and a certified copy of its Terms of Reference. - Certified copies of the minutes of all the committee’s meetings, along with its final report or recommendations on the alternative sites. - Certified copies of all relevant orders, file notings, recorded reasons and official correspondence on the decision to remove Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and designate alternative venues. Ravi Kumar Chaudhary, the Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) for the Union Territory (UT) Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs, replied to our application. He said that “upon consideration of the nature of the information sought and the potential implications of its disclosure, the information is exempted from disclosure under Section 8(1)(a) of the Right to Information Act, 2005.” Section 8(1)(a) allows information to be withheld if disclosing it could prejudice India’s sovereignty and integrity, the security of the state, or its strategic, scientific or economic interests. It also covers information that could harm relations with a foreign state or incite an offence. items.title: From 2,000 to 4.16 lakh a day: UP’s Form 6 applications surge after SSR draft electoral roll
items.summary: Following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Special Summary Revision (SSR) is now underway in Uttar Pradesh, with the stated objective of preparing an error-free electoral roll. An analysis of Form 6 applications by Alt News , however, reveals a sharp and unprecedented surge in applications for inclusion in the electoral roll, with daily submissions rising from a few thousand in early November to over four lakh by November 22. The SSR process began with the publication of the draft electoral rolls on November 17. About two weeks earlier, on October 30, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath had said at a BJP state working committee meeting in Lucknow that the names of around 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the electoral rolls. He urged party workers to launch a systematic campaign to ensure their inclusion. Again, on November 22, The Indian Express reported that the Uttar Pradesh BJP had instructed its workers to focus on Form 6 additions in the SSR to ensure inclusion of names of individuals eligible to be voters but left out during the SIR for some reason. Tracking Form 6 application data from the SSR process, Alt News found that between November 1 and 16, an average of around 10,000 applications were submitted daily across the state. The numbers began rising sharply from November 17, the day the draft rolls were published, and accelerated dramatically over the following five days. On November 22 alone, around 4.16 lakh applications were submitted. The numbers began rising the following day, with around 10,000 applications submitted on November 2. A similar number were filed on November 3 and 4, followed by 9,000 on November 5. items.title: Jensen Huang is back as CEO. The ethical questions aren’t over
items.summary: In about two weeks, Jensen Huang admitted to an affair, resigned from Nvidia, and got his job back. On November 8, he told employees in a memo that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The woman involved, Alice Huang, is a former executive at Megaspeed whom US officials believed was working for Chinese intelligence. Then the New York Times reported a relationship with Kimberly Powell, a vice president who reported directly to him, and Reuters reported one with a second employee. He resigned on November 12. On November 23, the board voted unanimously to bring him back. Much of the coverage treats all this as one scandal. It is really three separate questions. Was it wrong to cheat on his wife? Was it wrong to get involved with people who work under him? And did his relationship with Alice Huang put US national security at risk? The first is a private matter; Nvidia’s own rules should judge the second, and the third is the one the public has a real stake in. The marriage is private. The secrecy isn’t Jensen is 63 and married. Whatever happened in that marriage is for Jensen and his wife to deal with. But there is one caveat. An affair someone is trying to hide is a pressure point, and intelligence services look for pressure points. So the infidelity isn’t a public matter, but the secrecy around it becomes one once a foreign government might be involved. That point returns in the China section. Did Jensen follow his own company’s rules? Jensen’s workplace relationships are harder to judge, and there is no clean answer on consent once there is a power imbalance between the two people. Two adults can genuinely want to be together. The problem is that the junior employee may find it hard to say no, or to end things later, when the other person controls their reviews, promotions and projects. items.title: चार दशक पुरानी कार्टूनिस्टों की संस्था का इंस्टाग्राम अकाउंट भारत में प्रतिबंधित
items.summary: भारत के सबसे चर्चित राजनीतिक कार्टूनिस्टों में से एक की विरासत से जन्मी संस्था का डिजिटल मंच अब प्रतिबंधित कर दिया गया है. कार्टूनिस्ट्स कम्बाइन, एक ऐसा सामूहिक संगठन है, जो चार दशक से भी अधिक समय से कलाकारों को एक मंच पर लाने का काम कर रहा है. महाराष्ट्र में इस संस्था से 100 से ज्यादा कार्टूनिस्ट जुड़े हैं. इसकी स्थापना 1983 में बालासाहेब ठाकरे की पहल पर हुई थी. ठाकरे खुद भी एक राजनीतिक कार्टूनिस्ट थे. लेकिन 20 नवंबर को रात करीब 2 बजे इंस्टाग्राम ने भारत में इस संगठन के अकाउंट पर अस्थायी रूप से प्रतिबंध लगा दिया. संगठन के अध्यक्ष गौरव सर्जेराव ने बताया कि 19 नवंबर को इंस्टाग्राम की ओर से एक नोटिफिकेशन आया था. इसमें भारत में एक पोस्ट की पहुंच प्रतिबंधित किए जाने की जानकारी दी गई थी. साथ ही चेतावनी दी गई थी कि अगर संगठन इस तरह का कंटेंट साझा करना जारी रखता है, तो उसके अकाउंट पर भी प्रतिबंध लगाया जा सकता है. इस पोस्ट में एक कार्टून था, जिसमें प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी को एक ऐसे राजा के रूप में दिखाया गया था, जिसकी जिंदगी एक तोते पर निर्भर है. इस कार्टून में मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार को तोते के रूप में दिखाया गया था. सर्जेराव ने कहा, “मुझे नहीं पता कि अकाउंट इसी कार्टून की वजह से बंद किया गया है या नहीं, लेकिन हमें इसके संबंध में एक नोटिफिकेशन जरूर मिला था.” इंस्टाग्राम के नोटिफिकेशन में कहा गया था कि सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी अधिनियम (आईटी एक्ट) की धारा 73(b) के तहत सरकार या किसी कानून प्रवर्तन (लॉ एनफोर्समेंट) एजेंसी के अनुरोध पर यह प्रतिबंध लगाया गया है. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री ने मेटा इंडिया से संपर्क कर यह जानने की कोशिश की है कि किस एजेंसी ने यह अनुरोध किया था और इसके पीछे क्या वजह थी. जवाब मिलने पर इस रिपोर्ट को अपडेट किया जाएगा. सर्जेराव ने कहा कि संगठन अब इस कार्रवाई के खिलाफ आपत्ति दर्ज कराएगा और अकाउंट को पूरी तरह बहाल कराने के लिए “विरोध करेगा और लड़ाई लड़ेगा”. संगठन से जुड़े कार्टूनिस्ट रोहित कबाड़े ने बताया कि प्रतिबंध लगने से पहले 19 नवंबर को पोस्ट किया गया आखिरी कार्टून ‘लैपॉक्रेसी’ शीर्षक से था. उन्होंने यह कार्टून असम के मुख्यमंत्री हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा की उन टिप्पणियों के जवाब में बनाया था, जो सोनिया गांधी की किताब के विमोचन के बाद आई थीं. यह विवाद राहुल गांधी की उस टिप्पणी से जुड़ा था, जिसमें उन्होंने बताया था कि भोजन के दौरान उनकी मां अपने पिता की गोद में बैठती थीं. कार्टून में सरमा को प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी की गोद में बैठे दिखाया गया है, जबकि मोदी उद्योगपति गौतम अडाणी की गोद में बैठे हैं. संगठन के इंस्टाग्राम अकाउंट पर आमतौर पर कार्टून संबंधित कलाकारों के साथ कोलैबरेशन में पोस्ट किए जाते थे. सर्जेराव ने बताया कि उनका निजी इंस्टाग्राम अकाउंट भी 17 अक्टूबर को निलंबित कर दिया गया था. इसे बहाल कराने के लिए वह दिल्ली हाईकोर्ट में कानूनी लड़ाई लड़ रहे

items.title: NCDRC holds LIC liable for its agent's fraud after premium paid by customer diverted, misutilised
items.summary: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) recently held the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) vicariously liable for the misutilization and diversion of the premiums paid by a customer to one of its agents [Goldstar Diamond Pvt. Ltd. v Life Insurance Corporation of India Ltd. & Ors.] . A coram of President Justice AP Sahi and Member Bharatkumar Pandya ruled that the LIC was deficient in service for allowing premiums paid towards renewal of existing insurance policies to be diverted towards issuing new policies, causing financial loss to the policyholder. It added that LIC cannot escape liability merely because its agent had committed fraud, particularly when the premiums had been credited to and retained by the Corporation. "We therefore cannot segregate or divorce this relationship of principal and agent of the LIC with the OP-2 (LIC insurance agent), keeping in view the provisions of Section 182 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. If the agent committed some fraud with the LIC, the Corporation by retaining the amount continues to ratify the said fraud and would therefore be liable directly as well as vicariously for the acts and omissions of the OP-2," said the Commission. The case arose from a complaint filed by Goldstar Diamond, which had acquired insurance policies for its employees under an employer-employee scheme through one LIC agent Chetan Desai. The company alleged that Desai collected premiums for renewing existing policies but diverted the money towards issuing fresh policies without its knowledge. It paid over ₹7.90 crore in advance renewal premiums through cheques drawn in LIC's name, which were handed over to Desai. An internal investigation by LIC found several irregularities at its branch office, including failure to follow know-your-customer (KYC) requirements, bulk processing of policy applications and procedural lapses. The reports also recorded that Desai had admitted the fraud and acknowledged having used fake forms and forged documents. Considering the admissions made by Desai, the Commission in its November 16 order said that the Corporation was vicariously liable as it had retained the entire premium to its credit. "The Corporation therefore cannot escape its liability and in fact the loss suffered by the complainant in the manner aforesaid could not be disputed by the Corporation," observed the Commission. items.title: Criticise but don't defy: Madras High Court restrains protests against Supreme Court's Thiruparankundram lamp lighting order
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Tuesday passed an order restraining members of the public from calling for any defiance of the Supreme Court’s November 20 order permitting the lighting of a lamp to mark Karthigai Deepam (Hindu festival of lights) atop the Thiruparankundram hill this year. A Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi clarified such judicial directives can be criticised, even if it is sharp or strident criticism. The Court added that its order today only targets calls to prevent the implementation of the Supreme Court’s November 20 order. It made it clear the State authorities must ensure compliance with the order, and cannot afford to defy it merely because it has filed a review petition before the Supreme Court. The High Court held a pending review petition does not excuse non-compliance, while noting noted that the Supreme Court had passed no order on the review plea yet. District, police and temple officials, therefore, remain bound to implement the Supreme Court's November 20 directions, the High Court said. It added that Article 144 of the Constitution requires the Madurai Collector to act in aid of the Supreme Court. The High Court further told him to disregard any advice to flout the Supreme Court’s directions, even if it came from another authority. Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi The order was passed on pleas questioning restrictions imposed by a prohibitory order passed by the Madurai Collector preventing people from climbing or gathering near the Thiruparankundram hill during the Karthigai Deepam festival today. " We will just share our thoughts loudly. Feel free to interrupt ," the Bench said before issuing its directions. The High Court today held that the Collector’s prohibitory order under Section 163 of the BNSS must be applied in a manner that preserves the freedom of religion guaranteed under Article 25 of the Constitution. The High Court added that it expected the police to release without delay anyone who had been unlawfully detained under the prohibitory order, while closing the petitions before it. The two pleas before the Court challenged a prohibitory order issued by the District Collector under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) that restricted public gatherings and processions across Madurai district until 10 AM on November 25. items.title: Kerala High Court refuses to interfere with functioning of reconstituted State Waqf Board
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday refused to stay the State government's decision to reconstitute the Kerala State Waqf Board, observing that the newly appointed board had already assumed office and that its reconstitution would be subject to the final outcome of the pending petitions before a single-judge of the Court [CK Usman Haji v Union of India & ors and connected case]. A division bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was considering the appeals challenging a single-bench's order refusing to stay the government notification nominating new members to the board. The Court refused to stay the government's decision after observing that the new Waqf Board had already assumed office. " It is expressly admitted before us that the new Waqf Board has taken charge and that they are now in office. The learned single judge from the impugned order has made it clear that the reconstituted board will be subject to the outcome of the writ petitions. We are without doubt that this interim protection would be sufficient and that a stay of the government order at this stage would be untenable, " the Court added. However, it partly allowed the appeals by setting aside the single-judge's direction to refer the petitions to another Division Bench, which was hearing related cases concerning the composition of the Waqf Board. The Court explained that the reference was no longer necessary since those cases had already been disposed off. It accordingly directed the registry of the Court to list the writ petitions before the appropriate bench as per court roster. items.title: ITAT upholds tax benefits for Tata Sons on loans taken to fund investments in group companies
items.summary: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) in Mumbai has ruled that Tata Sons can claim interest paid on loans taken to invest in its group companies as a business expense, subject to restrictions on deductions relating to tax-free income [Tata Sons Vs DCIT]. Judicial Member Amit Shukla and Accountant Member GM Doss on October 29 held that the activities of Tata Sons extended beyond merely holding shares to earn dividends and that interest paid on borrowings for its investment-holding business qualified for deduction under the Income Tax Act. “ The assessee’s activities therefore extend beyond the passive holding of shares for the receipt of dividend ,” the ITAT observed. The dispute concerned the financial year 2013-14, during which Tata Sons incurred interest expenditure of ₹1,498.71 crore and other borrowing costs of ₹35.35 crore. During the same period, the company earned ₹4,387.19 crore in dividends and ₹453.29 crore in brand subscription fees. The Income Tax Department refused to allow Tata Sons to deduct interest paid on its borrowings from its taxable income on the ground that investing in group companies was not its business. The Assessing Officer also computed the disallowance of expenditure under Section 14A of the Income Tax Act at ₹1,522.40 crore. The provision prohibits deductions on expenses incurred in relation to tax-free income. Tata Sons challenged the decision before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), who allowed the deduction of interest expenditure and restricted the disallowance under Section 14A to ₹578.56 crore. Aggrieved, the Department approached the Tribunal. Tata Sons argued that its investments were not made solely to earn dividends. As the principal holding company of the Tata group, its business involved maintaining control over group companies, supporting their expansion and promoting new ventures. It also pointed out that it earned taxable income by licensing the Tata brand to group companies. Agreeing with Tata Sons, the Tribunal held that the purpose for which a company borrowed money must be examined in the context of its overall business activities. It further held that the mere fact that Tata Sons earned tax-free dividends did not justify denying deductions on its entire interest expenditure. “ The application of section 14A to expenditure relatable to exempt income does not, by itself, negate the business purpose of the borrowing or foreclose deduction of the balance expenditure ,” the Tribunal held. Gowda has now moved a fresh bail plea. In her petition, she has pointed out that the prosecution has examined 34 witnesses so far. Several witnesses are yet to be examined and the trial is likely to take considerable time to conclude, she highlighted. She has undertaken to cooperate with the trial and comply with any bail conditions imposed by the Court. She has further cited her family circumstances, stating that she is a single parent of a 17-year-old daughter pursuing her first year of pre-university education. items.title: Housekeeping staff at MNLU Nagpur end protest after contractor agrees to ESI cover, minimum wages
items.summary: Housekeeping staff at Maharashtra National Law University (MNLU), Nagpur have ended their six-day protest after the contractor agreed to Employees State Insurance (ESI) cover, minimum wages and full 30 days' pay. The workers, outsourced through the contractor, had begun their strike on November 18. They claimed that they were underpaid and that no Provident Fund (PF) or Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) contributions had been deducted or deposited for about three months. They also claimed that they were made to work extra hours and that their wages were paid in instalments, with half paid earlier and the balance released after Diwali. The absence of ESIC cover meant that one worker who sustained a chest injury on duty was meeting the cost of treatment himself. Another suffered a nail puncture to the foot and had received no benefit. The workers claimed that several letters to the Registrar and the Vice-Chancellor (VC) had drawn no effective response. They also wrote to the office of Commissioner of Labour seeking an investigation into the contractor. According to a student at MNLU, police personnel were deployed and patrolling had increased near the campus. The Superintendent of Police, Nagpur Gramin met the workers and had assured them that he will discuss the matter with VC Prof Jyoti Bhakare . They were told that the contractor will meet with them on November 23 to resolve their issues. In a November 21 press release, the University said that it had made sincere efforts to facilitate dialogue and an amicable resolution. "With over 1,300 students residing in the hostels and examinations scheduled to commence on 23 November 2026, maintaining basic hygiene and sanitation is essential. When attempts to engage alternative personnel to provide these essential services were obstructed, the University was compelled to seek police assistance to facilitate their entry into the hostels to maintain basic hygiene and sanitation," it stated. On November 23, during a joint meeting between the staff, the contractor, and the University administration, six demands of the staff were agreed to: Full 30 days' salary: Instead of 26 days' wages, they will now receive full 30 days' salary, inclusive of four weekly off days. items.title: Delhi High Court quashes suspension of lawyer who manhandled Justice Talwant Singh during BCD election
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently quashed the Bar Council of India (BCI's) suspension of advocate Deepak Tyagi after he tendered an unconditional apology for misbehaving with returning officer Justice Talwant Singh during the Bar Council of Delhi (BCD) elections. [ Deepak Tyagi v. Bar Council of India ]. Justice Amit Mahajan observed that the advocate gave an undertaking that he will not repeat unruly, disruptive or disrespectful behaviour inside the court premises, with any judicial officer or ex-judicial officer. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The BCI had placed Tyagi under interim suspension on February 27 this year over his conduct on February 22 during the Bar Council of Delhi elections. Tyagi was suspended from practicing before court, appearing or participating as an advocate during the pendency of the disciplinary proceedings. As per the allegations, on the polling day, Justice Singh proceeded towards the entry gate of the Delhi High Court after receiving complaints regarding violations of the Model Code of Conduct. At this time, Tyagi attempted to manhandle him and instigated a crowd of lawyers and raised slogans against the election machinery. The action was taken after the BCI received a suo motu complaint from the Special Committee of the BCD regarding the incident. "Any misbehaviour with, attempted manhandling of, intimidation of, or interference with the Returning Officer or the election process during a statutory Bar election strikes at the dignity of the legal profession and the integrity of the electoral process. Such conduct, if established, would amount to grave professional and other misconduct under the Advocates Act, 1961 and the Bar Council of India Rules," the Bar body said. Justice Talwant Singh Tyagi gave an express undertaking to the Court stating that he has tendered an unconditional apology for his conduct and that he has also apologised to Justice Singh, who accepted the same. The Court stated that no purpose would be served by continuing the suspension order and disciplinary action against the advocate. It thus quashed the BCI's suspension order. Advocates Sanjay Gupta, Surya Pratap Singh Chauhan, Shubhangam Thakur and Manoj Gupta represented Tyagi, who also appeared in person. Advocates Preet Pal Singh and Virat Raj Mishra appeared for BCI. items.title: Thiruparankundram Deepam lit at customary spot despite court orders
items.summary: Despite the Madras High Court directing the Tamil Nadu government to implement the Supreme Court's order to light the Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar near the Sikkandhar Dargah atop Thiruparankundram hill, the lamp was lit at the customary location near the Uchipillaiyar Temple on Tuesday, November 24, in keeping with a century-old practice. A bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and Sumathi of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, while hearing the matter on Tuesday, said the lamp must be lit at the stone pillar atop the hill in accordance with the Supreme Court's November 20 order, which had permitted the lighting as a “one-time arrangement”. “The authorities concerned are duty-bound to implement the Supreme Court's order. Even if advice contrary to the Supreme Court's order is given by any other authority, the District Collector should ignore it,” the judges said. They added that the filing of a review petition could not be cited as a reason for non-compliance. The judges also pointed out that the Supreme Court had stated in several orders that review petitions should not be filed with the intention of preventing the implementation of its directions. They directed the state government to clarify that it was prepared to comply with the Supreme Court's order and ordered the release of all those arrested in connection with the issue. On November 20, the Supreme Court had permitted the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the stone pillar near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah as a “one-time arrangement”, while clarifying that the decision should not be treated as a final judgment. During Tuesday's hearing before the Madurai Bench, the state government said that the structure atop the hill was a stone pillar. This came a day after the publication of a report prepared by the state's Archaeology Department, which identified the pillar near the Dargah as a Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) pillar erected during British rule. The map accompanying the report identified the original Deepathoon as being located below the Dargah. The report said that triangulation measurements taken during the current survey were consistent with those recorded in the colonial-era GTS report. These included bearings from Sikandarmalai hill station (Thiruparankundram) to stations such as Nagamalai, Sadragiri, Gopalswami, Kutiparai, Ponurikimalai and Perumalmalai. items.title: Why actor Sreejith TR was convicted in POCSO case: A closer look at the verdict
items.summary: A Thrissur court on Monday, November 23, sentenced Malayalam film actor Sreejith TR to one year of rigorous imprisonment in a sexual harassment case involving two minor girls. The two girls were subjected to sexual harassment by Sreejith on the porch of their apartment complex in July 2022. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 on him. The Special Fast Track Court-II, Thrissur, presided over by Judge Remya Menon, found Sreejith guilty under Section 11(i) read with Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, which deals with sexual harassment of a child and prescribes punishment for it, and Section 509 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which criminalises words or acts intended to insult a woman's modesty. However, the court applied Section 42 of the POCSO Act, under which the law prescribing the harsher punishment applies when an act is an offence under both laws. The court imposed the sentence only under the POCSO Act and did not award a separate sentence under Section 509 IPC. The court directed that the fine be paid as compensation equally to the two survivors. In default of payment, Sreejith will have to undergo an additional month of rigorous imprisonment. The period he spent in judicial custody from July 7 to 15, 2022, will also be deducted from his sentence. In its judgement, the court observed that the accused had targeted two school-going girls and that the incident had affected not only the children but also the society's sense of security. "The aggravating circumstance is that the convict had targeted two school-going girls, not only scarring the girls but also the society which depends on the decency of its members to trust their children to be on their own in public," the court said. What happened in July 2022 According to the prosecution, the incident took place around 3.20 pm on July 4, 2022, at the car porch of an apartment in Aranattukara, Thrissur, where the two girls lived. The girls, who were returning from school, were followed by Sreejith in a black Tata Safari. After reaching the apartment complex, he got out of the vehicle, exposed himself and engaged in an obscene act in the children's presence. The two girls, then aged 14 and 10, ran upstairs in fear and informed their parents about the incident. A complaint was lodged with the Thrissur Town West Police the same evening. items.title: Jana Sena leader Vangaveeti Radha sworn in as Vijayawada Mayor
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Vangaveeti Radhakrishna was sworn in as the 13th Mayor of the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation on Monday, November 23, with 85 of the 86 elected corporators also taking oath at Dr BR Ambedkar Kala Vedika. NTR District Collector and District Election Officer G Lakshmisha administered the oath to the Mayor and corporators. Sailaja Surabhi, the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) representative from Ward 32, was the only elected member absent from the ceremony. Following the swearing-in, the council conducted the election of the Deputy Mayor under the AP Municipal Corporations (Conduct of Election of Deputy Mayor) Rules, 2026. Chennupati Kanthisri, the TDP corporator from Ward 12, was elected unanimously. Her candidature was proposed by Ward 48 corporator Ummadi Venkateswara Rao and seconded by Ward 4 member Nandipati Devanand Kumar. The new council follows the November 1 municipal elections in which the NDA secured 76 of the 86 divisions. The TDP won 53 seats, JSP 19 and BJP four, while the YSRCP secured eight. The CPI(M) and an independent candidate won one seat each. Radha, who is the son of Kapu political leader Vangaveeti Ranga, has switched political allegiance over the years. After representing the Praja Rajyam party founded by actor Chiranjeevi in 2004, Radha joined the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) in 2014 and then the TDP in 2019. He finally joined Deputy Chief Minister Pawan-Kalyan-led Jana Sena Party (JSP) last month. Vijayawada MP Kesineni Sivanath, MLCs and other elected representatives attended the event. items.title: Unmasking misogyny: How a Malayalam YouTube channel weaponises science against women
items.summary: In July 2026, during a debate on 24 News’ Thammil Thammil about whether women should face restrictions on what they wear, a woman panellist posed a question that cut to the heart of the argument: If women’s clothes provoke sexual assault, what explains the rape of children and elderly women? Muhammed Ameer, an ‘educator’ and one of the prominent faces of the Malayalam digital platform Unmasking Anomalies (UA), had an answer. “Consider”, he said, “the amount of sexual imagery men are exposed to every day, from hoardings and advertisements to models.” A man sees a sexually exposed woman and becomes sexually frustrated. Just as someone who cannot shout back at a boss might take their anger out on someone at home, he argued, sexual frustration can be taken out on a different target. This, Ameer said, was “frustration-aggression theory”. When another panellist objected that this did not explain why women should change what they wear, Ameer was emphatic. “This is a psychological theory,” he asserted. “It’s not me saying this.” It is an effective way to make an argument, enough to make the person sitting across from you in a debate pause and reconsider what they can immediately challenge. Once a claim is attached to a psychological theory or a scientific study, it can easily begin to sound like a ‘fact’ rather than an opinion. The reaction in the comments under the video shows how deceptively powerful this method is. “The UA team never goes wrong wherever they participate. They have done thorough research,” one viewer wrote. Another described the women on the panel as “a group of ladies devoid of even the slightest trace of intelligence or awareness.” The women, after all, could not respond well enough to the ‘science’ being cited. But what happens when you follow that science back to its sources, and the argument doesn’t stand anymore? We will return to why Ameer’s claim does not hold up. Unmasking Anomalies, formerly known as Unmasking Atheism, is an Islamic theological group, primarily known for its debates and arguments with atheist and ex-Muslim critics.
